sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何地，非常感谢你收听这一期非常特别、且呼声极高的节目。

sentences.en: I think people have a lot of questions around this idea of trauma, not just in our 20s, but in our lives in general.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对“创伤”这个概念有很多疑问，不仅是在20岁时，在我们的整个人生中也是如此。

sentences.en: It is a super complex, nuanced space, and I think there are a lot of misconceptions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个超级复杂且微妙的领域，我认为存在很多误解。

sentences.en: We see the word trauma being thrown around quite casually, but what does it really mean from a psychological perspective?
sentences.zh: 我们看到“创伤”这个词被相当随意地使用，但从心理学角度来看，它到底意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: That's what we're here to kind of break down today, and I thought it would be important for us to bring on a very special guest, someone who knows this space well
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天想要剖析的内容，我认为邀请一位非常特别的嘉宾很重要，她对这个领域非常了解，

sentences.en: and who can really provide an evidence-based insight and opinion on some of the things we're going to discuss.
sentences.zh: 并且能为我们即将讨论的一些话题提供基于证据的见解和观点。

sentences.en: So without further ado, Dr. Mary Catherine McDonald, thank you so much for joining us, otherwise known as MC, of course.
sentences.zh: 那么，废话不多说，Mary Catherine McDonald博士，非常感谢你的加入，当然，大家也叫你MC。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我。

sentences.en: I'm so excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Yeah, when you reached out, I was like, this is the perfect person to have on the show because I do think that it's a question I get a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，当你联系我时，我就觉得你是节目最合适的嘉宾，因为我觉得这是一个我经常被问到的问题。

sentences.en: People are really fascinated by trauma.
sentences.zh: 人们对创伤非常着迷。

sentences.en: I think everyone has something that we could classify as trauma in their past, but a lot of the information we receive about it is through social media, is online.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人过去都有一些可以归类为创伤的事情，但我们接收到的很多相关信息都是通过社交媒体或网络获取的。

sentences.en: And sometimes that can make things, I think, more complicated rather than more accessible.
sentences.zh: 有时我认为这反而让事情变得更复杂，而不是更容易理解。

sentences.en: Do you want to give us a little bit of a background and an overview of what you do and how you came to kind of specialize in this area, in this domain?
sentences.zh: 你愿意给我们介绍一下你的背景，以及你是如何开始专注于这个领域的吗？

sentences.en: Yes, actually.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So I have a very kind of interesting path to trauma.
sentences.zh: 我进入创伤研究的路径非常有趣。

sentences.en: It was not the traditional way.
sentences.zh: 这不是传统的方式。

sentences.en: I have an interdisciplinary PhD, so I look at trauma from the perspective of philosophy, psychology, and neuroscience.
sentences.zh: 我拥有跨学科的博士学位，所以我从哲学、心理学和神经科学的角度来看待创伤。

sentences.en: And I started out looking at identity, and I wanted to think about what identity was composed of.
sentences.zh: 我最初研究的是身份认同，我想思考身份是由什么构成的。

sentences.en: And the specific thing that I was looking at is, like, to what extent is our psychology built in story form?
sentences.zh: 我当时研究的具体问题是：我们的心理在多大程度上是以故事的形式构建的？

sentences.en: And there was this huge debate in the philosophy of psychology at the time about that.
sentences.zh: 当时在心理哲学领域有一场巨大的争论。

sentences.en: And there was one side that was arguing that we are absolutely a coherent story, beginning, middle, and end.
sentences.zh: 一方认为我们绝对是一个连贯的故事，有开头、中间和结尾。

sentences.en: And all of our behaviors, for the most part, fit into a story, beginning, middle, and end.
sentences.zh: 我们所有的行为，在很大程度上，都符合一个有开头、中间和结尾的故事。

sentences.en: And it's how we organize the world.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们组织世界的方式。

sentences.en: And then on the other side, there was this smaller camp arguing that that was not true and that that was harmful.
sentences.zh: 而另一方是一个较小的阵营，他们认为那是不真实的，而且是有害的。

sentences.en: And that if you think of your life as a story, that you can actually cause psychological harm to yourself.
sentences.zh: 他们认为如果你把生活看作一个故事，实际上可能会对自己造成心理伤害。

sentences.en: That side, to me, seemed incorrect.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，那一方似乎是不正确的。

sentences.en: Like, of course, there's a way in which you could have too tight a story, and that could potentially be a problem
sentences.zh: 当然，你可能会把故事编得太紧，如果把身份与单一事物挂钩，那可能会产生问题，

sentences.en: if you're tying your identity to a singular thing that can cause issues.
sentences.zh: 这确实可能成为一个问题。

sentences.en: But it does seem to me to be true that our lives generally follow some kind of story form and that we're always telling a story.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，我们的生活通常遵循某种故事形式，而且我们总是在讲述一个故事，这似乎是真实的。

sentences.en: And so I reached for trauma, actually, because I thought it was a case that sort of proved that there is a story whether you identify with it or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我研究创伤，实际上是因为我认为这是一个案例，证明了无论你是否认同，故事都是存在的。

sentences.en: Because so many people, when they've been through a traumatic event, talk about how the story gets interrupted or shattered or broken.
sentences.zh: 因为当人们经历过创伤事件后，很多人会谈到故事是如何被中断、粉碎或破坏的。

sentences.en: And so I picked this up and really intended it to be a smaller argument and a larger argument about the nature of the self and identity.
sentences.zh: 所以我选择了这个课题，本意是想针对自我和身份的本质进行一个较小的论证，进而引出一个更大的论证。

sentences.en: And then I fell down this rabbit hole when I realized that the field of psychology still hadn't even decided what kinds of things counted as trauma and what kinds of things didn't.
sentences.zh: 然后我掉进了一个兔子洞，因为我意识到心理学领域甚至还没有决定哪些事情算作创伤，哪些不算。

sentences.en: And so as soon as I leaned into that, I just fell down this rabbit hole.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我深入研究，我就彻底掉进了这个兔子洞。

sentences.en: And then I started thinking like,
sentences.zh: 然后我开始想，

sentences.en: OK, we need to do this better.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们需要把这件事做得更好。

sentences.en: We need to get clear on what trauma actually is.
sentences.zh: 我们需要弄清楚创伤到底是什么。

sentences.en: And then I just sort of moved into the rabbit hole and I have been there ever since.
sentences.zh: 然后我就顺势进入了这个兔子洞，从此就一直待在那里。

sentences.en: It's my goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Pretty fascinating, pretty fascinating rabbit hole to be in, I would say.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常迷人的兔子洞，我想我会这么说。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I love that.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: It was an interesting time, sorry, to fall into the rabbit hole because at the time I was, you know, I was at Boston University, which is where Bessel van der Kolk was teaching.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，掉进这个兔子洞的时间点很有趣，因为当时我在波士顿大学，Bessel van der Kolk就在那里任教。

sentences.en: He wrote The Body Keeps the Score.
sentences.zh: 他写了《身体从未忘记》（The Body Keeps the Score）。

sentences.en: And yet when my professors heard that I wanted to focus on trauma as my research specialization, they said, you know, everyone knows that the trauma is made up.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我的教授们听说我想把创伤作为研究专长时，他们说，你知道，大家都知道创伤是编造出来的。

sentences.en: It's not real.
sentences.zh: 它不是真的。

sentences.en: These memories are planted in the minds of patients by the therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 这些记忆是治疗师植入病人脑海中的。

sentences.en: And this is, yeah, this was like, you know, 2010.
sentences.zh: 这可是，是的，这大概是2010年左右的事。

sentences.en: It wasn't like 1885.
sentences.zh: 又不是1885年。

sentences.en: So there's been this huge, like, resurgence of discussion, as you mentioned a minute ago, on social media and in society about, you know, the legitimacy of trauma.
sentences.zh: 所以正如你刚才提到的，社交媒体和社会上关于创伤合法性的讨论又重新兴起了。

sentences.en: But I think we have to be really, really careful and make sure that we're actually getting that conversation correct, you know.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们必须非常、非常小心，确保我们真正正确地进行了这场对话，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you really do owe it to,
sentences.zh: 而且你确实有责任，

sentences.en: I think everyone in society to not, to only say things such as what those people were saying and such as what those professors were saying when you're completely sure.
sentences.zh: 我认为社会上的每个人都有责任，只有在完全确定的时候，才能说出那些教授们所说的话。

sentences.en: I'm sure it probably came from a lot of Elizabeth Loftus' work as well around like implanted memories and false memories and things like that.
sentences.zh: 我相信这可能也源于Elizabeth Loftus关于植入记忆、虚假记忆等方面的研究。

sentences.en: But the idea that we actually don't have a good idea and a good description or categorization of trauma is one that I also find really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 但我们对创伤没有一个好的概念、描述或分类，这个想法本身也让我觉得非常迷人。

sentences.en: It's so interesting when you look at even the DSM or you look at the diagnoses that psychiatrists can give, it's like PTSD or complex PTSD.
sentences.zh: 当你查看《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）或精神科医生给出的诊断时，会发现这很有趣，比如创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）或复杂性创伤后应激障碍（C-PTSD）。

sentences.en: And that's kind of the two camps.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是两个阵营。

sentences.en: And it's like, but what does that really mean?
sentences.zh: 但那到底意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: Because each person is going to need a very, I think, unique path through that.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为每个人都需要一条非常独特的康复之路。

sentences.en: And I think that it is also this movement towards a more holistic way of seeing each individual's psychology, a more personal way of seeing each person's psychology
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这也是一种趋势，即以更全面的方式看待每个人的心理，以更个性化的方式看待每个人的心理，

sentences.en: and trauma is part of that.
sentences.zh: 而创伤是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: That kind of leads to this question that I have and I'm sure other people have, which is, what do you define as trauma?
sentences.zh: 这引出了我以及其他人可能都有的一个问题：你如何定义创伤？

sentences.en: Do you think there is any correct way of labeling a traumatic experience?
sentences.zh: 你认为有任何标记创伤经历的正确方法吗？

sentences.en: I do, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 有的，绝对有。

sentences.en: But I want to start actually with the incorrect way because I think that the field of psychology and psychiatry is actually getting this wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我实际上想先从错误的方法开始，因为我认为心理学和精神病学领域实际上在这一点上搞错了。

sentences.en: The incorrect way is to make a list of events and say, these things are traumatic and that's it.
sentences.zh: 错误的方法是列出一系列事件，然后说，这些事情是创伤性的，仅此而已。

sentences.en: So right now in the DSM, there are three things that are potentially traumatic.
sentences.zh: 所以现在在DSM中，有三类潜在的创伤事件。

sentences.en: There are three potential exposures that you can have to trauma.
sentences.zh: 你可以有三种潜在的创伤暴露。

sentences.en: One is actual or threatened death.
sentences.zh: 一是实际的或受威胁的死亡。

sentences.en: The second is serious injury.
sentences.zh: 二是严重伤害。

sentences.en: And the third is sexual violence.
sentences.zh: 三是性暴力。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这些。

sentences.en: Those are the three things.
sentences.zh: 就是这三件事。

sentences.en: And I think the reason that that's so problematic is because we miss entire populations of people who are showing up with all of the rest of the symptoms of PTSD
sentences.zh: 我认为这之所以如此成问题，是因为我们漏掉了整整一群人，他们表现出了PTSD的所有其余症状，

sentences.en: and not getting diagnosed correctly because they haven't met the criteria for traumatic stressor.
sentences.zh: 却因为不符合创伤应激源的标准而没有得到正确的诊断。

sentences.en: And I think it also reveals that we need to move away from trying to make a list and look instead at responses.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也表明我们需要摆脱试图列清单的做法，转而观察反应。

sentences.en: William James, who's sort of the father of modern psychology in many ways, described trauma as a thorn in the spirit.
sentences.zh: William James，在许多方面被认为是现代心理学之父，他将创伤描述为“精神中的一根刺”。

sentences.en: And I love this idea because it's a little bit vague, you know?
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个想法，因为它有点模糊，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And I think we can move from that and make it more specific so that we don't have this completely vague definition but that we also don't move to this thing where we're like,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以从那里出发，使其更具体，这样我们既不会有一个完全模糊的定义，也不会陷入那种境地，即我们说，

sentences.en: okay, these three things are traumatic and anything else is not.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这三件事是创伤，而其他任何事情都不是。

sentences.en: So the definition that I use is any experience that meets these two criteria.
sentences.zh: 所以我使用的定义是：任何符合这两个标准的经历。

sentences.en: You have an unbearable emotional experience, that's criteria one, that lacks a relational home, that's criteria two.
sentences.zh: 你有一种无法承受的情绪体验，这是标准一；它缺乏一个关系归宿，这是标准二。

sentences.en: And the reason I like this definition,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个定义的原因是，

sentences.en: I've adapted this from a clinician,
sentences.zh: 我从临床医生Robert Stolero那里改编了这个定义，

sentences.en: Robert Stolero,
sentences.zh: 但喜欢它的原因是，“无法承受”把门槛提得相当高。

sentences.en: but the reason I like it is because unbearable raises the bar pretty high.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能说你经历的每一件事、每一个小的不便、每一次你不高兴，你不能必然地说所有这些事情

sentences.en: So you can't say that every single experience that you're having, every minor inconvenience, every time you are upset, you can't necessarily say that all of those things
sentences.zh: 都是无法承受的。

sentences.en: are unbearable.
sentences.zh: 所以它使得被算作创伤的事物

sentences.en: So it makes it so that what counts as trauma
sentences.zh: 门槛足够高，这样我们就不会把这个词延伸到失去意义的地步，把所有事情都称为创伤，我认为我们正处于这种危险之中。

sentences.en: is sufficiently high so that we don't just kind of stretch the word to the point of meaninglessness and call everything trauma, which I think we're in danger of.
sentences.zh: 第二部分是，这种“关系归宿”的概念有助于我们理解，我认为，当我们接触到创伤时，我们需要什么来确保它不会变成

sentences.en: And the second part is that this idea of a relational home helps us understand, I think, both what we need when we've been exposed to trauma to make sure it doesn't become
sentences.zh: 持久的创伤，以及我们能给予彼此什么。

sentences.en: lasting trauma and also what we can give each other.
sentences.zh: 关系归宿的概念就是，我们的经历需要一个栖息之所，所有的经历都需要。

sentences.en: And the idea of a relational home is just that our experiences need a dwelling place and all of them do.
sentences.zh: 好的经历、平庸的经历，它们都需要一个栖息之所。

sentences.en: Good experiences, mediocre experiences, all of them need a dwelling place.
sentences.zh: 当它们太令人难以承受，以至于我们在自己内心找不到栖息之所时，我们需要其他人来关联这些事件，帮助我们弄清楚把它们放在哪里。

sentences.en: When they're too overwhelming for us to find a dwelling place within ourselves, we need other people to relate the event to, to help us figure out where to put it.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 这在某种意义上是在提供心理上的了结吗，你觉得？

sentences.en: Is that kind of like, is that in a sense providing psychological closure, do you think?
sentences.zh: 可以是，是的。

sentences.en: It can be, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你在想一个具体的例子吗？

sentences.en: Were you thinking of a particular example?
sentences.zh: 是的，不，我只是在尝试，因为当我们谈论“关系”时，我认为，
